# Validation report

<!-- Generated by tools/validation-report.R. Do not edit by hand: CI regenerates this file and fails if it differs. -->

**11 of 11** published workbook values reproduced, 3 deliberate differences, 0 failures.

Every figure in the `mixdra` column was produced by re-fitting the reference datasets with the current version of the package. The `workbook` column comes from [`inst/validation/oracles.csv`](inst/validation/oracles.csv), which records each published value together with the sheet and column it was read from, and which is also what the test suite asserts against. A number cannot appear here without being tested, or be tested without appearing here.

**Diff** is the distance from the published value. **Tol.** is how much of the allowed tolerance that distance uses — a low percentage is a strong agreement, near 100% only just qualifies. Rows marked – make no point-value claim; their bounds are asserted in the test suite instead.

## Binary CPF + MPs, concentration addition, continuous response

`binary_mps_cpf_ca_continuous`

| EC50 CPF (C1) [^binary_mps_cpf_ca_continuous-1] | `0.094` | `0.093529` | 0.5% | 10% | ✓ |
| Residual SS (reference) [^binary_mps_cpf_ca_continuous-2] | `1 633 769` | `2 224 215` | 36% | <0.1% | ✓ |
| Selected deviation [^binary_mps_cpf_ca_continuous-3] | `DL` | `DL` |  |  | ✓ |

[^binary_mps_cpf_ca_continuous-1]: *single-compound curve.* EC50 of the toxic component taken from its own single-compound curve.

[^binary_mps_cpf_ca_continuous-2]: *workbook joint fit.* The workbook re-fits the curve parameters on the mixture data, which absorbs interaction into the curves and lowers its residual. This engine fixes the curves on the singles, so its reference residual is necessarily higher.

[^binary_mps_cpf_ca_continuous-3]: *workbook model selection.* Dose-level deviation; agrees with the workbook.

[^ternary_fbsa_cpf_imi-1]: *per-ratio sheets / 'Advanced S/A' column.* Stage-1 base fitted from singles + control.

[^ternary_fbsa_cpf_imi-2]: *workbook fixes EC50 FBSA at 5.58.* Held fixed in both the workbook and this fit; agreement here is by construction and is not an independent check.

[^ternary_fbsa_cpf_imi-3]: *workbook beta2 spans ~13-56 across its fits.* Weakly identified because EC50 FBSA is pinned. Only the sign and magnitude are checked (must exceed 10); no point value is claimed.

[^ternary_fbsa_cpf_imi-4]: *sheet 'Overall' col G.* Stage-2 fit from the binaries with the base held fixed — exactly the workbook's own design. Sign must be positive (synergy).

[^ternary_fbsa_cpf_imi-5]: *sheet 'Overall' col G.* Sign must be negative (antagonism).

[^ternary_fbsa_cpf_imi-6]: *sheet 'Overall' col G.* Sign must be negative (antagonism).

[^ternary_fbsa_cpf_imi-7]: *workbook pure-CA residual SS (df 412).* Must sit below the workbook's pure-CA residual — adding interaction terms can only reduce it — while staying the same order of magnitude.

## What this report does not show

Two implementations agreeing shows that they agree. It does not show that either is right. That is what the synthetic recovery tests are for: data is generated forward from known parameters through the same model the fitter uses, and the engine has to invert it back to those parameters. Those live in [`tests/testthat/test-recovery.R`](tests/testthat/test-recovery.R).

Reference data are *Folsomia candida* soil reproduction assays (chlorpyrifos, microplastics, imidacloprid and FBSA, in mg/kg), fitted with the Jonker et al. (2005) mixture dose-response method.
